sample.universe: Children in grades 0 through 8 whose households were provided municipal 'urgent needs' social housing in Copenhagen in 2009-2014, plus comparison populations of children living in social housing and of all children within a 15-minute walk of social housing in Copenhagen
selection_rules: Household contacts the municipality with a housing problem and is screened by a social counselor as having 'urgent needs'
Household reaches the top of the queue for one of the every-third vacant social housing units reserved for urgent-need households and receives a first housing offer in 2009-2014
Child is in grades 0 through 8 at the time of the assignment
Child can be observed with the relevant outcome (so sample sizes vary across outcomes)
sample.period: housing assignments 2009-2014; outcomes measured up to December 31, 2021 (education), March 2023 (earnings), December 2018 (mental illness)
sample.n_observations: 1,134 children in the main quasi-randomly assigned sample; 1,072 for the education/earnings/index outcomes, 1,134 for crime outcomes, 1,199 for the mental illness outcome; comparison groups of 4,040-4,518 children in social housing and 222,333-263,796 children within a 15-minute walk

construction_notes: Neighborhoods are defined by OpenStreetMap walking distance from the residence (1 to 15 minutes); the main scales are 2, 5, 10 and 15 minutes.

The text reports that the 2-minute definition averages 561 neighbors, the 5-minute 3,031, the 10-minute 11,642 and the 15-minute 25,748; the note to Table 2 instead reports average populations of 454, 2,252, 8,872 and 20,608 residents for the same four scales.
All neighborhood quality measures are calculated immediately prior to the household's new housing assignment and scaled to mean zero, standard deviation one.
The summary index of neighborhood quality combines average neighborhood income, employment and education using Anderson (2008), with the sign of unemployment switched so higher values are better.
Alternative neighborhood quality measures: share ethnic minority (non-western origin), children's test scores, share of adults charged with a crime (safety).

The summary index of child outcomes is an Anderson (2008) index of the six outcomes, mean zero and standard deviation one in the population of children within a 15-minute walk, with negative outcomes reverse-scaled.
Earnings are the sum of all salary income including employee benefits from age 18 to March 2023, in 2023 U.S. dollars.
All outcomes are measured in the most recent year of data; cohort fixed effects for year of housing assignment control for the different durations over which outcomes are measured.
Standard errors are clustered at the family level because some families contribute more than one child.
